LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
Sourcing this PKGBUILD for `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only executes top-level scope, which here consists solely of standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `optdepends`, `conflicts`), the `source` array, the `sha256sums` array, and two function definitions (`pkgver`, `package`). No command substitution, backticks, `eval`, `curl`/`wget`, or other executable statements appear in the global scope, so nothing downloads, executes, or exfiltrates data while the file is parsed.

The `source` entry is a git clone of the package's own declared upstream (`https://github.com/por-cli/por-cli.git`), which is expected for a `-git` package, and `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is normal practice for VCS sources and irrelevant to this gate since no sources are fetched during `--printsrcinfo`. The bodies of `pkgver()` and `package()` (including the `git` calls and `install` commands) are only defined, not run, at this step and are out of scope for this narrow gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Only standard variable and function definitions; no top-level code execution.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a straightforward `-git` VCS package. The only source is the declared upstream repository (`git+https://github.com/por-cli/por-cli.git`), and `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is required/expected for a VCS source, so it is not evidence of tampering. The `pkgver()` function runs routine `git rev-list`/`git rev-parse` commands to derive a version string, and `package()` simply installs the upstream `por-cli` script (`install -Dm755`) and its `LICENSE` (`install -Dm644`) into `$pkgdir`. Both actions are standard packaging practice.

There are no network fetches from unexpected hosts, no `curl`/`wget` piping to a shell, no `eval` or base64/hex-obfuscated payloads, no writes outside `$pkgdir`, and no attempts to read or exfiltrate local data. The declared runtime dependencies (curl, fzf, mpv, yt-dlp, etc.) match the stated purpose of a CLI media browser. Only minor hygiene notes apply: the source tracks a mutable branch (normal for `-git`), and no `build()` step exists, which is acceptable since the package installs a shell script directly.

No malicious or dangerous behavior was found.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard -git PKGBUILD; upstream source, no malicious code found.</summary>
</security_assessment>

The source is a git URL pointing to the project's own GitHub repository (https://github.com/por-cli/por-cli), which is standard practice for `-git` packages. The `sha256sums = SKIP` is expected and required for VCS sources. The dependencies (bash, curl, fzf, mpv, chafa, yt-dlp, jq, sed, grep, gawk, coreutils, libnotify) are all legitimate CLI tools consistent with the stated purpose of a terminal-based media browser. No executable code, suspicious network operations, obfuscation, or injected malicious behavior is present in this metadata file.
</details>
